question: An 8-year-old boy is brought to the physician by his father because of abnormal movements of his limbs. For the past four days, he has had uncontrolled jerking movements of his arms and legs and has been dropping cups and toys. His symptoms are worse when he is excited and improve while he is asleep. During the same time period, he has become increasingly irritable and tearful. He had a sore throat 6 weeks ago that resolved without treatment. His temperature is 37.3°C (99.2°F). Examination shows occasional grimacing with involuntary jerking movements of his limbs. Muscle strength and tone are decreased in all extremities. When he grips the physician's index and middle fingers with his hands, his grip increases and decreases continuously. This patient is at increased risk for which of the following complications?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Group A Streptococcus infection -> Rheumatic fever -> Sydenham chorea -> 80% CHAIN: Sydenham chorea -> Decreased muscle strength and tone -> 70% CHAIN: Decreased muscle strength and tone -> Risk for extraneural metastasis -> 60% CHAIN: Risk for extraneural metastasis -> Complication in the patient -> 50% CHAIN: Complication in the patient -> Increased risk for extraneural metastasis -> 40% CHAIN: Increased risk for extraneural metastasis -> Extraneural metastasis -> 30% CHAIN: Extraneural metastasis -> Complications -> 20% CHAIN: Complications -> Increased risk for extraneural metastasis -> 80%
enhanced_information: The patient's presentation with abnormal movements, irritability, and a history of a sore throat 6 weeks ago is consistent with Sydenham chorea, a complication of Group A Streptococcus infection. Sydenham chorea can lead to decreased muscle strength and tone, but it does not increase the risk for extraneural metastasis. Therefore, the patient is not at increased risk for extraneural metastasis as a complication.
